Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Parasram on 13 August,
2024
Author: Anil Verma

Bench: Anil Verma
Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Ind:23401 1
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Anil Verma
 On The 13th Of August, 2024
 Misc. Appeal No. 2421 of 2014
 (Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd.
 Vs
 Parasram & others)
Appearance:

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (Shri Pankaj Kumar Jain Advocate for appellant)
(Shri Sanjay Karanjewala Advocate for respondent No.3)
Heard finally with consent of both the parties.

1/ The appellant has preferred this Misc. Appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (in short MV Act) being aggrieved by the impugned award dated 21.8.2014 passed by II Additional MACT Jaora District Ratlam in claim case No. 11/2013, whereby a sum of Rs. 1,97,000/- has been awarded to the claimants.

entities.text: II Additional MACT Jaora District Ratlam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2 Brief facts of the case are that on 9.5.2011 at about 9.30 pm when respondent/claimant was driving his vehicle carefully at that time respondent no. 1 who is driver of offending vehicle bearing registration No. MP-09--FA-2237 rushly and negligently driven the vehicle and hit the claimant due to which claimant sustained injuries.
Claimant has lodged an FIR at police station Alot.

Accordingly offence under Section 279, 337 of IPC has been registered against respondent no. 1 and at the time Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Parasram on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83595927/

entities.text: Shriram General Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Parasram on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 of accident the vehicle was insured with appellant/insurance company.

3 The claimant has filed a claim case under Pectin 166 of Motor Vehicles Act by stating that due to accident he got two fractures in his right leg and his primary treatment has been done in government hospital Alot and thereafter he was referred to District Hospital Ratlam, thereafter he was admitted in Patidar Orthopedic Hospital Ujjain.
He was doing the work of labour and agriculture and was earning Rs. 2 lakhs per year.
Hence he claimed for payment of compensation of Rs. 7,20,000/-.
4 Respondents no. 2 and 3 both were remained absent before the below tribunal.
5 The appellant/insurance company has denied all the claim averments by stating in written statement that at the time of accident, the vehicle owner was not having any effective and valid permit.
The accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle/respondent no. 2.
The offending vehicle was not insured with the appellant company therefore, the appellant company is not liable to pay compensation.

6 The below Tribunal after framing the issues and after appreciating the evidence available on record, allowed the claim petition by passing an award of Rs. 1,97,000/- along with interest @ 7.5%
per annum.
Being aggrieved by the findings given by the below Tribunal, this appeal has been preferred by the appellant.
7 Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the impugned award passed by the below tribunal is against law and facts.
The below tribunal has ignored the pleadings and evidence adduced by the appellant.

The below tribunal has come to the conclusion that permit was not valid on the date of accident, but kept the issue its effect on the liability of appellant company open to be decided by the appellant himself and thereby failed to decide the issue No. 4 and 5.

The below tribunal has committed an error in not considering the fact that claimant has not suffered any permanent disability and excessive award has been passed, hence he prays that impugned award be set aside.
8 On the other hand, counsel for respondent no. 3 opposes the prayer by submitting that the impugned award passed by below tribunal is just and proper and does not deserve for any interference.
9 Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record with due care.

10 So far as the awarded amount is concerned the respondent no.1./claimant has proved bills Ex.
P-10 to Ex.P-31 for his treatment and x-ray bill Ex. P-34 amounting to Rs. 56,831/-.

11 From perusal of the statement of claimant Parasram (PW-2), it is proved that he sustained multiple fracture in right tibia fibula bone and after operation rod was inserted and he remained admitted in the hospital for period of about 15 days, therefore, the below tribunal has rightly awarded compensation of Rs. 10,000/- under the head of pain and suffering and Rs. 18,000/- for loss of income.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Dr. O.P. Gupta (PW-1) also proved that claimant Parasram became unable to do any work from his right leg for the period of two years, his permanent disability has been assessed 12% therefore,
looking to the age of claimant (38 years), multiplier of 15 was correctly applied by below tribunal and accordingly assessment of Rs. 97,200 for future income appears to be just.

Additional Rs.
10,000/- has been rightly awarded to the claimant for his future loss therefore, the amount of Rs.
1,97,000/- is just and proper which cannot be said to be excessive in view of the injuries sustained by claimant.

13 But the main contention of counsel for appellant is that at the time of accident, owner of offending vehicle was not having any effective and valid permit, therefore, due to breach of insurance policy appellant is not held liable for payment of any compensation amount.

Before the below tribunal the appellant has examined Administrative Claim Officer Mukesh Kanade (DW-1)
who categorically stated that due to breach of insurance policy, the insurance company is not liable for any compensation.
Anish (DW-2) who is owner of offending vehicle has produced fitness certificate Ex. D-2 which has been issued for period of 20.8.2010 to 19.8.2011.
Admittedly the accident was occurred on 9.5.2011.

The claimant did not produce any relevant document for permit of offending vehicle at the time of accident, therefore, on the basis of fitness certificate Ex. D-2 it is proved that at the time of accident his vehicle was used without any fitness certificate and permit.

14 In the matter of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Papaiah 2006 ACJ 126 (Karnataka), Hon'ble Division Bench of Karnataka High Court in a case where autorickshaw met with an accident at a place 20 km away from police station whereas its permit permitted it to be plied within the radius of 10 km of the town, it was held that there is breach of permit conditions and terms of the policy and the insurance company exempted from its liability.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Papaiah 2006 ACJ 126 (Karnataka)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Division Bench of Karnataka High Court
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However, it was directed that insurance company has to pay compensation awarded to the third party and recover the amount from the insured.

Similar view has been taken by the coordinate Bench of this court in case of Sunita Vs.
Asgar Ali 2010ACJ 126.
15

In view of the aforesaid position of law, this court is of the considered opinion that the below tribunal has committed error in not directing the insurance company to deposit the amount with a right to recover from respondents no. 2 and 3.
Therefore, para 37 of impugned award relating to liability of insurance company deserves to be modified but rest of award remains intact.

16 In view of the aforesaid, the appeal filed by appellant/insurance company is partly allowed by holding that the awarded amount of Rs. 1,97,000/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum shall be deposited by appellant/insurance company with below tribunal with a right to recover the said amount from respondents no. 2 and 3.

The below tribunal is directed to invest 80% of said amount on long term fixed deposit in the name of claimant Parasram in nearest Nationalized Bank, in the area where the claimant is residing, with a further direction that bank will not permit any loan or advance and interest on said amount will be paid on quarterly basis directly to the claimant.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ BHUNESHWAR DATT 2024.08.14 19:19:15 +05'30'
